paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption: : Majority voting.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how majority voting accuracy varies as the number of completions \(k\) increases, showing multiple accuracy curves across the same axes. The x-axis is labeled “Number of completions (\(k\))” and uses a logarithmic base-2 scale with tick labels at \(2^0, 2^1, \ldots, 2^8\) (from \(2^0\) to \(2^8\) at regular exponent steps of 1). The y-axis is labeled “Majority voting accuracy,” is on a linear scale, and spans approximately from 0.24 up to just above 0.60, with labeled ticks at 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, and 0.6. One dark blue solid line with circular markers starts near 0.43 at \(2^0\) and \(2^1\), rises to about 0.49 at \(2^2\), ~0.53 at \(2^3\), ~0.57 at \(2^4\), ~0.59 at \(2^5\), ~0.60 at \(2^6\), and reaches about 0.61 by \(2^7\)–\(2^8\). A dark green solid line with upward-triangle markers closely follows a similar upward pattern, beginning near 0.43 at \(2^0\)–\(2^1\), increasing to around 0.50 at \(2^2\), ~0.54 at \(2^3\), ~0.57 at \(2^4\), ~0.59 at \(2^5\), ~0.60 at \(2^6\), and ending around 0.61–0.62 by \(2^7\)–\(2^8\).
